concepts.def: A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Numbers & The Number System — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Numbers & The Number System brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Numbers & The Number System.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
